description: Substrate parameter q₀ pinned to 50 decimal digits via mpmath.  READ THE THREE anchor_* ROLE FIELDS BELOW BEFORE USING THIS: the word "anchor" does three different jobs in this witness and they do NOT all say the same thing.  This producer is listed under ideal_muon in q0_anchor_manifest.json, so when run under its own name q_parameter rebinds q_at to return the MUON literal and the Newton solve described below never executes -- derived_50_digit.q is the muon value.  The m_p/m_e route is what DEFINES the quantity, not what ran.  Internal arithmetic is exact to 50 digits; physical anchoring is bounded by the propagated CODATA relative uncertainty ≈ 8.30e-13 (830 ppQ) from the 0.017 ppb m_p/m_e ratio (see physical_anchoring_bound).  m_μ/m_e is recorded only as a 9.5σ cross-check prediction.  Recorded 50-digit outputs: q, q^{-1}, ℏ_q², ℏ_q, H_A, [2]_q, z_markov, s_skein; plus quantum integers/factorials and n=3 Plancherel weights.  ξ(q₀) via Bring-curve λ is NOT yet recorded — the current placeholder has been disabled; port lambda_bring_q0.py to 50 digits and re-emit.

calibration_inputs.anchor_role: DERIVATION ROUTE — the identity that defines q0. NOT the layer emitted: under the ideal_muon manifest entry this run returns the muon literal and this solve does not execute. For the emitted layer read q0Anchor (muon).

universal_shape_coupling.reason: bring_lambda() placeholder disabled to prevent unreliable xi(q₀) values.  Port the verified lambda_bring_q0.py derivation to 50-digit mpmath before re-enabling.

physical_anchoring_bound.comment: Internal arithmetic is at 50 digits.  The framework's DIMENSIONLESS predictions (ratios, equality of computed quantities) can be checked at 50-digit precision.  q₀ is anchored on m_p/m_e (the most precise ratio, 0.017 ppb); the propagated bound σ(q₀)/q₀ ≈ 8.30e-13 (830 ppQ) improves one-for-one as CODATA improves m_p/m_e — it is not a framework ceiling.  The muon-anchor bound (~1.22e-9) is shown for comparison and is ~429× looser; m_μ/m_e is now a 9.5σ prediction.
